title: Spotify stays connected while its grant is alive, and a failed refresh is retryable unless the grant is dead (packet 3)
acceptance: C-1, web: a Spotify connection whose access token has expired is still 'connected' everywhere the SPA reads connection state (providerConnectionState in apps/web/src/lib/providers.ts): Live preflight and the coordinator, Music, Connections, Songs and the builder no longer show Spotify as 'Session expired' or ask to reconnect just because an hour passed. The server already refreshes on use (mintSpotifyPlaybackToken, user-likes, user-playlists). Apple Music's expiry handling is unchanged (D27); SoundCloud's existing exemption stays. The coordinator test that expects an expired Spotify connection to be no_connected_provider is updated to the new contract.

C-2, package: the Spotify token endpoint failure (packages/music/src/spotify-oauth.ts postToken) throws a typed error that keeps the HTTP status and the OAuth error code (for example invalid_grant), without the response body text or any token.

A dead grant (OAuth invalid_grant) is remembered: the server clears that connection's stored refresh token (only on invalid_grant, never on Ritmo-side errors such as invalid_client, and only if it is still the token that was refused, so a concurrent rotation survives), GET /providers/connections reports refreshable: false, and the SPA then shows Spotify as Session expired with Reconnect and preflight treats it as not connected.

C-2, API: one shared helper classifies a failed refresh in all three places that refresh (spotify-playback-token.ts, user-likes.ts, user-playlists.ts). A dead grant (400/401, invalid_grant, a missing or undecryptable refresh token) stays 409 REAUTH_REQUIRED. A Spotify 5xx, a network failure or a malformed token response becomes the retryable 502 provider error, and a 429 becomes the retryable 429. Neither starts OAuth.

C-2, web: a retryable failure from the playback-token request during a Spotify start or the SDK's token callback shows a retryable playback error (Live's existing Retry path), never a Reconnect Spotify prompt; REAUTH_REQUIRED and PLAYBACK_REAUTH_REQUIRED keep their current messages.

Tests: docs/audits/codex-code-audit-2026-10-27-4e0b150/repro/c-web-playback-repro.test.ts and c-api-token-refresh-repro.test.ts are adapted to the new contract and pass as unit or integration tests in the repo's suites. Integration tests drive the playback-token route against a fake token endpoint for 400 invalid_grant, 500, 503, 429 and a thrown fetch.

Contract: the OpenAPI entry for GET /providers/spotify/playback-token documents the 502 and 429 responses, regenerated with no drift. The PR tells the Neo, because the native Mac Live uses this route and should treat 502/429 as retry, not reconnect.

Owner set this task Ready in the Air session, 2026-11-12.

Implementation. Local gate on 2026-11-12 (Air): format, owner-gate/rf-trace/tasks tests, tasks:check, typecheck, eslint, design-system verify, theme-classes, pnpm test (web 1,784 tests; API unit incl. new refresh-failure, token-error and playback-token cases), API integration incl. 5 new playback-token cases against a fake Spotify token endpoint, web build within budget (178.32 kB gzip), OpenAPI regenerated, contract-parity clean, audit:ci. Playwright e2e not run locally (Chromium not installed on this machine); CI runs it. No real Spotify playback verified: that is RF-217.

Final review on 29145e4 (2026-11-12) found a significant regression: a revoked Spotify grant showed Connected with no Reconnect. The owner approved the fix ("Fix it"): the server forgets a refused refresh token, MusicConnectionView gains optional refreshable, and the web shows Spotify expired only when expiresAt passed and refreshable is false. Token-fetch network failures are now a typed status-0 error, so a code TypeError is no longer called an outage. Local gate after the fix: format, owner-gate/rf-trace tests, tasks:check, typecheck, eslint, theme-classes, pnpm test, API integration (14 playback-token cases incl. refused-grant DB/view check and the rotation race), web build, OpenAPI regenerated, contract-parity clean, audit:ci. e2e left to CI.

Final review on 8a07973 (2026-11-12) found a significant data-loss risk: any 4xx except 429 cleared stored refresh tokens, so a rotated client secret (400 invalid_client) would wipe every user's grant. Fixed: only OAuth invalid_grant clears the token; other 4xx still answer 409 without deleting. Unit and integration tests cover invalid_client keeping the token.

resolution: Spotify's hourly access-token expiry no longer reads as a disconnect in the SPA (Live preflight, Music, Connections, Songs, builder); a dead grant (OAuth invalid_grant) clears the stored refresh token so the connection view reports refreshable: false and the SPA shows Session expired with Reconnect (TrackSearch also passes reauthRequired on a 409). Both OAuth clients throw ProviderTokenError with status and OAuth error code; one refreshFailure helper maps a refused grant to 409 REAUTH_REQUIRED, a Spotify 429 to the 429 quota error and 5xx/network/malformed bodies to the 502 provider error, at all three refresh sites. On web, a temporary token failure gets one quiet retry in the SDK callback and is worded as Retry, not reconnect. OpenAPI and api.md document the 502/429. The owner's browser check after a deploy is RF-217.
